claims.text: As-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 is a eutectic high-entropy alloy with a fine lamellar FCC/B2 microstructure.
As-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 has low room-temperature tensile ductility and undergoes catastrophic interfacial cracking.
SPS at 1300°C using gas-atomized, low-oxygen powder can produce a fully dense specimen.
HPT of AlCoCrFeNi2.1 at 1400°C and 200 MPa will impose severe plastic deformation without cracking.
Sequential SPS and HPT will transform the lamellar FCC/B2 structure into a patterned ultrafine-grained configuration.
The treated AlCoCrFeNi2.1 microstructure will have a grain size below 500 nm.
HPT will disrupt and reconfigure the continuous lamellar FCC/B2 interfaces into a more isotropic arrangement.
The reconfigured microstructure will impede interfacial crack propagation and be more defect tolerant.
Breaking down continuous lamellar interfaces will reduce interfacial stress concentrations.
The treatment will promote dislocation cross-slip and grain-boundary sliding.
Cross-slip and grain-boundary sliding will promote uniform plasticity and enhance room-temperature ductility.
Grain refinement will maintain or slightly improve yield strength relative to the as-cast alloy.
The treatment will produce greater than 20% room-temperature tensile elongation.
The treatment will increase fracture toughness and eliminate catastrophic interfacial cracking.
Oxygen content must remain below 0.1 wt% to avoid oxygen-induced brittleness.
Processing above 1400°C would cause phase instability or excessive grain growth.
Maintaining 200 MPa is necessary to obtain full densification without cracking.
Vacuum SPS limits oxygen uptake, whereas the HIP comparison uses an argon pressure medium.
A conventional HIP control will process the same alloy at 1400°C, 200 MPa, and 2 h without SPS or HPT.
Failure of the HIP-only control to alter the lamellae or improve ductility would falsify the claim that HPT is necessary.

contradictions.description: The starting state is specified as an as-cast bulk alloy, but the required treatment is specified to begin with gas-atomized powder followed by SPS. These are different starting material forms and processing histories.

If HIP without HPT leaves the lamellae intact and does not improve ductility, that result supports rather than falsifies the claim that HPT-specific deformation is necessary. A decisive falsification would require HIP alone to reproduce the patterned microstructure and mechanical improvement, or HPT to fail under the proposed conditions.

Both HPT and HIP are assigned the same nominal pressure of 200 MPa, while only HPT supplies torsional shear strain. Thus the comparison isolates torsional severe plastic deformation more directly than it isolates an effect of 'extreme pressure.'
